title: Thermal Energy
seo_title: Grade 3 Science: Thermal Energy Worksheets (BC Curriculum)
standard_text: Thermal energy can be produced and transferred: sources of thermal energy (chemical reactions, friction, the Sun), thermal energy as the movement of particles, and transfer by conduction, convection and radiation. (summary of BC's Curriculum, Science 3, Physics)
meta_desc: Free Grade 3 science worksheets (BC): heat and temperature, sources of heat, conduction, convection and radiation, and conductors and insulators. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Heat moves from warmer to cooler things.
body_html:
How to think about it

Thermal energy is the energy of moving particles: the faster they move, the hotter something is. Heat can come from the Sun, from burning fuel, from chemical reactions (hand warmers) and from friction (rubbing your hands).

Heat moves in three ways: conduction (through touching, like a hot spoon), convection (moving liquids and gases, like warm air rising) and radiation (through space, like sunlight). Conductors such as metal let heat through easily; insulators such as wool slow it down.

Example

Why do your hands get warm when you rub them?

Rubbing makes friction.

Answer: friction makes heat

Example

Which keeps a drink cold longer: a metal cup or a foam cup?

Foam is an insulator.

Answer: a foam cup

Common mistakes

  • Saying cold moves into things (heat moves out).
  • Thinking a sweater makes heat (it traps your heat).
  • Mixing up conduction and convection.

faq.q: How does the Sun's heat reach Earth?
faq.a: By radiation, which can travel through empty space.

faq.q: Why are pot handles made of plastic or wood?
faq.a: They are insulators, so heat does not reach your hand.

items.q: A hot iron touches a cotton shirt. In which direction does heat flow?
c: from a hot iron to a cotton shirt
from a cotton shirt to a hot iron
items.e: Heat flows from a hotter object to a colder one.

items.q: Which way does heat flow?
c: from a warmer object to a cooler one
from a cooler object to a warmer one
items.e: Cold is not a thing that flows.

items.q: Why are pot handles made of plastic or wood?
c: They are insulators, so they do not conduct heat to your hand.
items.e: Insulators slow heat flow.

items.q: Maya compares two things. Which has a higher temperature: a bathtub of warm water (40 °C) or a cup of hot tea (80 °C)?
items.e: Temperature measures the average motion of the particles.

items.q: Kai compares two things. Which has a higher temperature: a big pot of soup (60 °C) or a spoonful of the same soup (60 °C)?

items.e: Both are 60 °C, so the particles have the same average energy.

items.q: A sea breeze blows towards land on a sunny day. Which type of heat transfer is this mainly?
items.e: Conduction: through solids by particles vibrating. Convection: in liquids and gases as warm fluid rises. Radiation: infrared waves, even through a vacuum.

items.q: A sea breeze blows from the sea towards the land in the afternoon. Which process mainly transfers the heat?

items.q: A thermos keeps soup hot. How?

It is made of conducting metal only.

items.q: What happens to the particles of a substance when it is heated?
c: They move faster and spread out.
items.e: This is why most things expand when heated.

items.q: Why does a dark car get hotter in the sun than a white car?
c: Dark colours absorb more radiant energy.
items.e: Light colours reflect radiation.
